zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 9; they obstruct the downward and outward view from balconies on Decks 10, 11, and 12, with Deck 10 experiencing the most severe obstruction.
zones.effect: Balconies look directly at or over orange lifeboat covers instead of open water down to the waterline; the horizon remains clear but the romantic 'look down at the ocean' view is blocked.
zones.mattersTo: Matters greatly to first-time cruisers and photographers who imagine an unobstructed ocean view; experienced cruisers and those who spend little time on the balcony often don't mind, especially given the price advantage.

zones.what: The Y-shaped hull design extends the midship superstructure outward past the lifeboat line, creating wider balconies with unobstructed side views.
zones.effect: Midship balconies on these decks cantilever beyond the hull giving wider lateral sightlines past the lifeboats and a more stable ride than higher or end cabins, typically at a lower price point than upper decks.
zones.mattersTo: Value-focused cruisers seeking balcony space and stability without premium pricing; less relevant to those prioritizing height or aft views.

zones.what: The main pool deck (Deck 17 aft) sits directly above with sun loungers, music, and poolside activity throughout the day.
zones.effect: Expect daytime noise from pool activities, music, and foot traffic overhead from mid-morning through evening; vibration from deck furniture being moved.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and those wanting quiet daytime cabin time should avoid; night owls and those out exploring the ship all day won't notice.

zones.what: The open-air sports deck and activity area (Deck 22) sits directly overhead with basketball, shuffleboard, and running track.
zones.effect: Daytime noise from bouncing balls, running footsteps, and sports activity; mostly quiet after evening hours.
zones.mattersTo: Daytime nappers and remote workers will be disturbed; those using the cabin only for sleeping won't care.

zones.what: The two-deck Europa Theater spans Decks 7 and 8 directly below the forward cabin sections.
zones.effect: Low-frequency sound from theater performances and shows can transmit upward, particularly during evening showtimes; Deck 11 is closer and more affected than Deck 14.
zones.mattersTo: Early-to-bed guests in forward cabins on Deck 11 may hear muffled bass during 9-10pm shows; Deck 14 is far enough that most won't notice.

zones.what: The World Galleria (shopping promenade) and main dining rooms on Deck 15 sit directly below.
zones.effect: Ambient noise from dining service, music, and foot traffic until approximately 11pm; chair scraping and conversation carry upward during dinner hours.
zones.mattersTo: Guests turning in at 9-10pm may hear activity below; late diners and night owls won't be in the cabin during the noise.

zones.what: Deck 5 cabins sit low in the hull where bow thruster vibration is noticeable during maneuvering (docking and tendering) and anchor chain noise occurs at port arrivals.
zones.effect: Rumbling vibration during port arrivals and departures, typically early morning; the anchor chain creates loud mechanical sounds when deployed or retrieved.
zones.mattersTo: Extremely relevant to light sleepers who will be awakened on port days; heavy sleepers and early risers are unaffected.

zones.what: The 'Promenade Balcony' and 'Promenade View' cabins face inward to the ship's internal World Promenade rather than the ocean.
zones.effect: Balconies overlook the indoor shopping and dining street with pedestrian traffic, ambient music, and retail activity; no ocean view but protected from weather and often discounted.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to those expecting ocean views who didn't read the category name carefully; a deliberate choice for people-watchers and those prioritizing price over seascape.

zones.what: MSC Yacht Club exclusive decks with restricted access via dedicated elevators and keycard-controlled areas.
zones.effect: Quieter environment with less through-traffic and smaller guest population; proximity to private Yacht Club facilities but farther from main ship amenities.
zones.mattersTo: Yacht Club guests value the exclusivity and separation; those wanting to be near main dining and entertainment should consider lower decks.
